THE ODIANA ADOPTION, INTEGRATION, AND EXPANSION CANON Adoption, Lineage Integration, Demography, and Expansion Law of the Ide Igbo (Iwu Nnabata Omu n’Odiana Ide) Status: Sacred–Civic Canon Authority: Odiana • Seven Uniku • Ide Igbo Scope: 100-Year Civilisational Horizon Nature: Guardianship-based, lawful, non-coercive

PREAMBLE Life is a trust of Ana, not a possession of blood alone. Where lineage fails through war, famine, or collapse, Odiana permits rebirth through guardianship, so that no child of black ancestry stands without a hearth. Adoption in Ide is not charity. It is continuity.

BOOK I — PURPOSE, ELIGIBILITY, AND LIMITS OF ADOPTION

ARTICLE I — PURPOSE OF ADOPTION

  • To preserve life endangered by war, displacement, or social collapse.
  • To strengthen the Seven Uniku without creating new clans.
  • To bind adopted children permanently to Ide law, land, and moral order.
  • To ensure every adopted child becomes Ide by nurture, law, and rite, not by force.

ARTICLE II — ELIGIBILITY

Section 1: Eligible Children A child may be received if:

  • orphaned, abandoned, or lawfully released for adoption;
  • guardianship is legally transferred;
  • Adoption serves the child’s welfare first.

Section 2: Prohibitions

  • No child taken without consent.
  • No adoption for labour, tribute, or servitude.
  • No erasure of origin; history is recorded.

Violation constitutes Ikpu Alu (civic and ritual crime).

ARTICLE III — AGE OF ENTRY

  • Primary intake: Omuazi (0–6 years)
  • Secondary intake (restricted): early Omuaka (7–9)
  • Older children may reside as wards, not lineage-adoptees.

This preserves psychological and cultural coherence.

ARTICLE IV — UNIKU ASSIGNMENT

  • Every adopted child is assigned to one of the Seven Uniku.
  • Assignment is:
  • numerically balanced,
  • reviewed annually,
  • recorded in Uniku archives.
  • Identity format: Omu–[Uniku].
  • Adoption never creates a new Uniku, sub-Uniku, or Ogbe.

Uniku are eternal and finite.

ARTICLE V — RITES OF INCORPORATION

Each adopted child undergoes:

  • Ndose Rite of Reception
  • Naming in Ide dialect
  • Registration in Uniku rolls
  • Household guardianship oath

From this moment, the child is indistinguishable in law from birth-born Ide.

ARTICLE VI — RIGHTS AND DUTIES

Rights

  • inheritance within household
  • education
  • protection by Omunna, Omuada, Ndose courts
  • marriage within Ide

Duties

  • obedience to Ide law
  • defence of Ide land
  • reverence for the Seven Ogbe of Ide Igbo
  • preservation of Odiana and Ide culture

ARTICLE VII — LIMITS

  • Adopted lineages may not claim Uniku headship.
  • They may hold office except Ikala and Agbalanze.
  • Loyalty to Ide Igbo supersedes all prior affiliations.

BOOK II — UNIKU ADOPTION QUOTAS

ARTICLE VIII — BASE QUOTA

  • Total: 240 children per year
  • Per Uniku: ~34 children per year

Maintains:

  • demographic balance
  • cultural density
  • administrative control

ARTICLE IX — ADJUSTED QUOTAS

Expansion Phase

  • +25–40% quota
  • children earmarked for frontier Obo

Stabilisation Phase

  • quota temporarily reduced

Reviewed every 5 years by the Ndose Adoption Council.

ARTICLE X — LIFETIME CEILING

  • Adoption-descended Ide may never exceed 30% of total population.
  • Prevents dilution and elite displacement anxiety.

BOOK III — AGE-GRADE INTEGRATION MODEL Omuazi (0–6)

  • Ide dialect immersion
  • Odiana rituals
  • Ndose health and care
  • No labour

Outcome: identity imprinting

Omuaka (7–12)

  • Communal schooling (Ndose-run)
  • Farm literacy and design literacy
  • Ide and Igbo history

Outcome: moral and cultural anchoring

Omunti (13–17)

  • Discipline, respect, self-respect, and personal boundary camps
  • Craft, manufacturing, trade, exchange, material culture, and agriculture
  • Odiana ethics
  • Uniku loyalty training

Outcome: identity sealed; outsiders feel foreign

Omuaro (18–30)

  • Marriage eligibility
  • Frontier deployment
  • Obo founding units
  • Military and civic duty

Outcome: expansion engine of civilisation

BOOK IV — ADOPTION FLOW TO EXPANSION FRONTIERS Tier 1 — Ide Igbo (Years 0–2)

  • intake
  • health screening
  • rites
  • language immersion

Tier 2 — Uniku Training Obo (Years 3–15)

  • agrarian towns
  • education hubs
  • identity deepening

Tier 3 — Frontier Obo (Omuaro age)

  • farming blocs
  • construction teams
  • civic foundations

Rule: no adopted group founds an independent town.

BOOK V — MARRIAGE AND LINEAGE INTEGRATION

ARTICLE XI — BLOOD INTERWEAVING PRINCIPLE

  • Adoption is incomplete without marital integration.
  • Adopted Ide are honour-bound, not forced, to marry into:
  • Ide direct lineages
  • core Uniku families
  • Odiana-linked households

ARTICLE XII — UNIKU MARRIAGE REGISTERS

Each Uniku maintains Obibi Uniku, containing:

  • lineage classification
  • permitted and preferred marriage paths
  • prohibited unions
  • integration priorities

Supervised by Omunna, Omuada, and Ndose. Advisory only; consent remains absolute.

ARTICLE XIII — ROYAL LINEAGE (AGBILI-IDENZE)

  • Numerically limited
  • Ritually guarded
  • Politically supreme

Marriage into Agbili-Idenze is:

  • rare
  • strategic
  • elite-approved

Royal supremacy without social cruelty.

ARTICLE XIV — INCENTIVES

Aligned marriages receive:

  • land priority
  • housing grants
  • business capital
  • education subsidies
  • ceremonial elevation

No penalties for refusal.

BOOK VI — WEALTH AND WELFARE (ODIANA DOCTRINE)

ARTICLE XV — POVERTY IS ALU

  • Poverty is disorder, not virtue.
  • No Ide citizen may fall into destitution.

Core Mechanisms

  • Land guarantee (housing and farmland)
  • Universal Ndose services (health, education, care)
  • Uniku Prosperity Trusts (capital, relief, start-ups)
  • Soft wealth ceiling (hoarding censured, circulation honoured)

CANONICAL POPULATION AND EXPANSION STRUCTURE

EARLY POPULATION MODEL (FIRST 20–30 YEARS) Canon Clarification (Locked)

  • Years 0–20/30:
  • Only Ide Igbo (the first Obo) exists
  • Population produced: 2,500–3,000
  • Intentionally slow-grown
  • Purpose: identity density, not numbers

This population becomes the biological, cultural, and institutional benchmark.

YEAR 0–20 / 30 — IDE IGBO ONLY Political Completion at Adulthood (18 years):

  • Ikala and Iyi crowned
  • Agbalanze (Ikala kingmakers) established
  • Otu Enyi (Iyi queenmakers) established
  • Parliament members established
  • Otu Nze (men’s entrepreneurial titles)
  • Otu Odu (women’s maritime-heavy equivalent)

Settlement

  • 1 Obo: Ide Igbo
  • 7 Ogbe → roots of Seven Uniku
  • No satellite towns

Population

  • 2,500–3,000 total
  • Birth-born Ide and adopted Omuazi/early Omuaka

Age-Grade Distribution

  • Omuazi: 25–30%
  • Omuaka: 30%
  • Omunti: 20%
  • Omuaro: 20–25%

ADDENDUM VII — FIRST UNIKU OBO FORMATION After 20–30 years:

  • Each Uniku forms its first Obo
  • Each targets a population of 2,500–3,000

Structure:

  • Ide Igbo (ancestral hearth)
  • 7 Uniku Obo (parallel towns)

Population:

  • Ide Igbo: ~3,000
  • 7 × 2,750 ≈ 19,250
  • Total: ~22,000

ADDENDUM VIII — BIRTH RATE AND FERTILITY MODEL Marriage Structure

  • 50% monogamous
  • 50% polygamous
  • Max wives: 4

Monogamous Households

  • 5–7 children (avg. 6)

Polygamous Households

  • 17–22 children (avg. 17)

Growth Effect

  • Average per household: ~11–12
  • Generation length: ~20 years
  • Controlled, compounding growth

ADDENDUM IX — ROYAL AND KINGMAKER STRUCTURE

  • IDENZE → IKALA (male supreme sovereign)
  • OMU (Omumu) → IYI (female supreme counterpart)
  • No other clan is royal.

ADDENDUM X — EZEME CLAN (NON-NEGOTIABLE) Ezeme functions:

  • commerce
  • finance
  • markets
  • infrastructure
  • trade networks
  • capital formation
  • guilds and banking logic

Every Obo must contain an Ezeme quarter.

ADDENDUM XI — CLAN PRESENCE PER OBO Mandatory:

  • Ezeme — economy
  • Akuana — agriculture
  • Dilibe — health
  • Anaka — religion/education
  • Oviaeli — security
  • Ulide — culture
  • Oyiora — governance

ADDENDUM XII — IDEANA RULE (FRONTIER OBO) Any Ide who:

  • fights for Ide identity
  • establishes an Obo
  • secures land and people

may rule as Ideana, with rotation among founders and Agbili-Idenze.

ADDENDUM XV — FULL 100-YEAR DEMOGRAPHIC MODEL

  • Year 0–20: ~3,000
  • Year 20–30: ~22,000
  • Year 30–50: 140,000–175,000
  • Year 50–75: 1.2–1.5 million
  • Year 75–100: 4.2–5.25 million

ADDENDUM XVI — LEGAL CODEX OF EZEME ECONOMIC AUTHORITY (Iwu Aku na Avia Ide) Ezeme is the sole economic authority, kingmaker, and legitimising power, never the Ideana, preserving separation of power and civilisational stability.

FINAL CONFIRMATION

All core structures remain intact:

  • Ide Igbo as eternal hearth
  • Seven Ogbe → Seven Uniku → all Obo
  • Ezeme as royal-economic clan
  • Idenze and Omu as kingmakers
  • Odiana welfare doctrine
  • Adoption, marriage, demographic, and expansion rules
